FAQ & Reference
Start the server
Shevery runs a privileged server (root, ADB, or wireless debugging) so approved apps can access system APIs and remembers your last launch mode.
On Home, start via Root (libshizuku.so), Wireless debugging, or the exact PC/OTG adb shell command shown on screen. Enable Start on boot in Settings → Application for automatic recovery.

Uninstall the official Shizuku Manager first because package IDs conflict. Without root or autostart, ADB-started servers stop after reboot; wireless autostart waits up to 120s for unlock on non-TV devices.
Wireless debugging
Start Shevery over local ADB without a PC on Android 11+, with optional TCP-5555 mode and boot-time re-enable.
Connect to Wi-Fi, enable Wireless debugging in Developer options, and follow the in-app pairing tutorial with both the pairing port and 6-digit code. Tap Start on Home once paired.
The pairing port differs from the connection port. Keep the screen awake during pairing, grant Nearby Wi-Fi (Android 13+) or Local Network (Android 17+), and pair only on trusted networks.
Comput terminal
Built-in shell console executing commands through the active Shevery server with live colored output, Presets, JSON Macros, history, and in-output search.

Start the server and open Terminal. Run commands directly, pick a preset, record macros, or enable ADB mode to strip host adb shell prefixes automatically. Tap Stop to cancel a running command (exit 124).
Commands run with the server’s ADB shell or root privileges. On-device adb install should use pm install; host-side push/pull or device listing still requires a computer.
Commandium AI
Turns plain-language goals into Android toybox shell commands and explains failed command output in Comput.

Open Settings → AI → AI provider to pick one of 11 presets (Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, etc.) or a custom OpenAI-compatible URL. Open Commandium from Comput or tap Explain with AI on errors.
API keys are encrypted in AndroidKeyStore (AES/GCM), but prompts and failed command outputs are sent to your active provider. Keep secrets out of prompts and keep ReCommand enabled.
Comput AI Agent
Interactive multi-step assistant in Comput that plans up to 10 shell or ADB module service steps, runs them with approval gates, saves chat history, and summarizes findings.

Open Comput → Agent, describe your goal, and choose Secure (approve every step), Turbo (auto-run), or Custom (3/5/10 max steps and per-type prompts) in Settings → AI. Use History to resume any saved chat.
Desktop tools (apt, systemctl, iptables) are blocked in favor of Android toybox commands. Always review or edit commands with Allow / Edit & Allow before running in Secure or Custom mode.
ADB modules
ZIP-packaged shell and WebUI extensions unpacked into Shevery’s private adb_modules storage and executed via the active ADB or root server (no Magisk mount hooks).

Install a ZIP with module.prop at the root from ADB Modules, a file manager Share/View intent, or the Catalog. Modules can expose action.sh (e.g. ShizuConfig’s diagnostics Action), service.sh, and webui/index.html using $MODDIR.
Install limits: max 2048 entries, 200 MB extracted, 256 KB per script, 120s script timeout (exit 124), 64 KB retained logs. Inspect scripts before running; do not assume /data/adb/modules paths.
Module catalog
Discovers GitHub repositories tagged shevery-modules (cached 6h, max 4 per author except HmnDev-Tech) and installs modules from Sources or Release ZIPs.

Open Catalog from ADB Modules, filter by stars or recency, and inspect details before installing. Configure Sources vs Release ZIP mode and an optional GitHub PAT in Settings → Updates → Module updates.
Anonymous GitHub search is capped at 60 req/h; a ghp_ or github_pat_ token raises it to 5000 req/h and is stored in EncryptedSharedPreferences, sent only to api.github.com.
App and module updates
Checks GitHub Releases for Shevery self-updates (Stable or Beta) and resolves module updates across updateJson, catalog metadata, and GitHub releases.
In Settings → Updates, pick Stable or Beta and Daily, Weekly, or Manual WorkManager checks, or check manually. Module update checks compare versionCode first and run from ADB Modules.
Beta includes pre-releases. App updates stream to a PackageInstaller session, so Android still asks for confirmation unless Device Owner handles silent install; always review module changelogs first.
Device Owner & Dhizuku
Manages Device/Profile Owner activation, 5 DPM app delegation scopes, ownership transfer, native Dhizuku API v1/v2 serving, and experimental Dhizuku bridge mode.

Open Settings → Device Owner to activate in 1 tap via Shizuku or copy the adb shell dpm command. Manage delegations or Strict Whitelist Mode under App Delegation, or enable Dhizuku Mode in Settings → Application after starting Shevery first.

Device Owner requires no conflicting accounts during initial dpm setup and affects device-wide policies. Deactivating uses a 5s safety countdown; never start Shevery through Dhizuku before Shevery is running.
Security & authentication
Locks Shevery and individual sensitive actions behind BiometricPrompt or device credential with configurable session timeouts.

Open Settings → Security, enable authentication, pick a timeout (Immediately to 1 hour), and choose protected actions: app launch, Device Owner/transfer, app permissions, server start/stop, and stub install/removal.
When a session expires in the background, Shevery locks on return and drops temporary grants from that session. Keep at least one lock screen credential configured on the device.
Compatibility stubs
Installs lightweight bridge APKs (moe.shizuku.privileged.api and com.rosan.dhizuku) so legacy apps that hardcode package-name checks work with Shevery.
Open Settings → Application → Compatibility Stubs and tap Install. StubManager automatically tries Device Owner, active Shevery Server, Root, and Local ADB channels in order.
Stubs use the original package IDs, so Android cannot install them alongside the original Shizuku or Dhizuku apps. Stub actions can be biometric-protected under Settings → Security.
Stealth Edition generator
On-device APK rebuilder (Android 10+) that clones the bundled stealth template with a random com.<8>.<8> package ID and custom launcher label.

Create a backup in Settings → Backups first, then open Settings → Application → Stealth version. Customize the app and file name, save to Downloads/, uninstall standard Shevery, and install the generated APK.

Stealth APKs keep Shevery’s binder provider authorities, so standard Shevery must be uninstalled before installing the stealth copy. Back up first so you can restore settings, grants, and modules in one tap.
ErrorProtect watchdog
Monitors server main-thread heartbeats (5s beat / 60s freeze limit) and system binder deaths (package, activity, user, appops) so the native starter daemon recovers cleanly.
ErrorProtect is on by default in Settings → Application. It rebinds dead system services with 5s–60s backoff (up to 10 tries) or restarts shizuku_server via the detached starter supervisor.
Crash-loop protection stops after 5 consecutive rapid failures, resetting after 60s of stable uptime. Disable ErrorProtect only if an external tool manages the server lifecycle.
Hide Developer options
Temporarily toggles off device-wide Developer options whenever selected apps come to the foreground and restores it afterward.
Open the tool from Extras/Lab, grant Usage access (PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS), ensure Shevery or Device Owner is active, and enable switches for target apps.
The setting is global while active and may affect debugging tools. If Shevery is force-stopped mid-session, reopen Shevery so it restores the original state.
Hide USB debugging
Polls the foreground app every second when unlocked and hides Settings.Global.ADB_ENABLED for banking, payment, or DRM apps.
Grant Usage access, start Shevery or set Device Owner (WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS), and select target apps. Shevery saves and restores ADB_ENABLED automatically on app switch or screen lock.
Disabling ADB_ENABLED affects the whole device and can drop active USB/ADB connections while the target app is open. Reopen Shevery to recover if force-stopped.
Network firewall
Blocks per-app internet access without using Android’s VPN slot by driving the built-in eBPF connectivity chain3 through Shevery’s shell.
Requires Android 13+ AOSP connectivity chain3 and a running Shevery server. Toggle blocking per app; Shevery verifies kernel :deny/:allow state via cmd connectivity.
The system chain3 policy is shared across Android, so enabling it may activate other rules and blocking a package affects all apps sharing its Android UID.
Shevery Connectors
Gates both the connector ContentProvider (content://moe.shizuku.privileged.api.connector) for LPE activators and incoming Tasker/MacroDroid automation broadcasts.
Enable Shevery Connectors in Settings → Automation after reviewing the safety prompt. Activators query the command column; automation tools check live status in View intents.
Off by default for safety. While enabled, any app that reads the connector or holds your auth token can control the server; disable Connectors when not needed.
App authorization
Controls which third-party apps hold elevated Binder IPC permissions via RequestPermissionActivity and server-side FLAG_ALLOWED/FLAG_DENIED flags.
Start the server, approve or deny apps when prompted, and audit or revoke grants anytime in Authorized apps on Home.

Never grant access to untrusted apps. Revoking blocks future API calls but cannot revert system changes already made. On Android 8.0+ ADB, non-Activity apps need a transparent Activity once for binder delivery.
Tasker & MacroDroid
Automates Start, Stop, Restart, and Toggle server actions plus a Server is running state condition via the Locale/Tasker plugin or explicit broadcasts.

Enable Connectors in Settings → Automation. Use the Shevery Tasker plugin in Tasker, or send explicit broadcasts to com.hamondev.shevery / PluginReceiver with extra auth=<token> in MacroDroid or Termux.
Missing or wrong auth tokens return RESULT_CANCELED and post an alert notification. Regenerating the token invalidates all existing macros; non-root START_SERVER needs ADB TCP enabled first.
Automation & public intents
Documents public automation broadcasts, RequestPermission, Accessibility Manager shortcut, Module WebUI deep links (shevery://module/<id>), and ZIP VIEW/SEND intake.

Copy ready-made am broadcast commands from Settings → Automation or Home → View intents. Launch WebUIs via shevery://module/<id> or OPEN_WEBUI, and open Accessibility Manager via ACCESSIBILITY_MANAGER.
Internal SheveryControlReceiver actions are non-exported and fail from adb shell. ModuleWebViewActivity omits BROWSABLE to block untrusted web iframes and enforces APP_OPEN auth if enabled.
Settings
Organizes 11 sections: Application, Appearance, Security, Device Owner, Modules, Updates, AI, Backups, Automation, Extras, and About.
Configure boot startup, ErrorProtect, and TCP port in Application; Black theme and Classic nav in Appearance; ZIP export/restore in Backups; Accessibility Manager with keep-alive pinning in Extras.
Backup ZIPs can contain preferences, app authorizations, AI settings, and installed modules—store exported archives privately.
Module access policy
Per-feature gate controlling Action scripts, background service.sh, WebUI JS shell bridge, WebView internet, and WebUI downloads (SAFE / CUSTOM / FULL).
Keep SAFE (manual actions only) by default, or switch to CUSTOM for granular permissions in Settings → Modules. Long-press a module card to grant or revoke Full Trust.

WebView internet is blocked even in FULL mode unless CUSTOM enables it or the module is trusted. Full Trust is bound to installed files and auto-revokes if the module payload changes; keep ReCommand on.
Lab & gestures
Houses Shake-for-Guide sensitivity presets and live counter, pure Black night theme, Reduced expressive motion, and IPC binder snapshots.
Open Settings → Lab to pick Low/Medium/High shake sensitivity, run the live shake test, toggle Black night or Reduced motion, or inspect current Shizuku/Shevery/Connector binder state.
Running the shake calibration test temporarily pauses automatic guide opening so you can test hits cleanly. IPC snapshot exports status only without logcat dumps.
FAQ & troubleshooting
Covers Shizuku package conflicts, wireless pairing failures, server drops, scam renames, module install rejections, and Smart Logs.

For wireless pairing, enter both the pairing port and code. For drops, keep ErrorProtect on and exempt Shevery from battery optimization. Use Smart Logs on Home or verbose logging in Extras for issues, and ShizuConfig’s Action in Catalog for device diagnostics.
Shevery is 100% free—avoid paid downloaders and fake renames like Shizako+. Strip tokens and personal data before attaching logs to GitHub issues.
How Shevery works
Forwards app system API calls over Binder IPC (transactRemote) through a privileged server, avoiding slow per-command su shell spawning.
Start shizuku_server via ADB or root, let BinderSender deliver the binder as apps launch, and use ShizukuBinderWrapper plus Android17Compat fallbacks for Android 15–17 signature changes.
Available permissions match the server UID (shell for ADB, root for su). Normal apps on Android 9+ still need hidden-API bypasses for restricted platform methods.
Publish a module
Any public GitHub repository with module.prop and the shevery-modules topic appears automatically in Shevery’s Catalog within the 6h cache window.
Place module.prop at repo root (or a validated subdir), add the shevery-modules GitHub topic, optionally host updateJson, and attach a ZIP matching the module ID for Release installs.
Keep the module id stable, bump versionCode every release, stay within the 4-module per-author catalog limit, and keep scripts readable so users can audit them.
Build from source
Builds the Compose manager app, Rust/NDK native binaries, server, starter, and compatibility stubs from the HmnDev-Tech/shevery repository.
Run git clone --recurse-submodules, configure JDK 21 / Android SDK / NDK & Rust targets, and run ./gradlew :manager:assembleDebug or :manager:assembleRelease.

Cloning without --recurse-submodules fails the build. Debug builds produce a debuggable shizuku_server; installing over an existing APK requires a matching signing key, and Apache 2.0 trademark rules bar reusing Shevery branding.
